method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the statements the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. The rule in the article's code block is ours (the engine's fvg rule plus a clock filter), not a quotation from any of these pages.

definition_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: ICT Silver Bullet [LuxAlgo]
what_it_says: Three windows in New York local time: London open 03:00 to 04:00, AM session 10:00 to 11:00, PM session 14:00 to 15:00.
Works with fair value gaps formed during the window; a gap that has not been retraced by the end of the session is made invisible.
Minimum distance settings: 40 ticks for index futures or indices, 15 pips for forex pairs, described as the best-case expected price delivery and not the actual entry-to-exit range.
Says to use anything below the 15-minute timeframe; its examples use the 3-minute timeframe.
No performance statistics.

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Silver Bullet
what_it_says: An ICT setup defined by the clock: a specific one-hour window in which the trader looks for a single trade. Three windows, all anchored to New York time: 3 to 4 am, 10 to 11 am, 2 to 3 pm.

Inside the window, wait for the manipulation (a sweep of a mapped liquidity pool, or a clear structure shift), then enter on a fair value gap created by displacement inside the window. If no valid gap forms before the window closes, no trade.
Stop beyond the swing that formed the manipulation, or beyond the far edge of the entry gap in tighter variants. Target: the opposing liquidity pool identified before the window.
'No audited public statistics exist, and claimed win rates circulating online should be treated as marketing until shown otherwise.'
'instruments without a meaningful New York cadence, most crypto included, fit it poorly.'
Says the model was popularized through Michael J. Huddleston's ICT content in the early 2020s. It does not give a minimum gap size or a timeframe.

definition_sources.name: AudaCity Capital: ICT Silver Bullet Strategy: Windows, Setup and Execution Rules
what_it_says: Same three windows, in New York local time. 'The setup must form inside the window.' A trade can be opened during the window and take considerably longer to reach the opposite liquidity pool.
Mark liquidity on the 15-minute chart before the window; execute on a 1, 3 or 5-minute chart (its example uses 3 minutes).
Confirming a market structure shift is described as a step some sources skip.

Stop: just past the candle that created the gap, or past the swing from the sweep. Target: the opposite liquidity pool, or a fixed reward-to-risk multiple in some sources. No required ratio or stop buffer is stated as a rule.
Reports that a 55% to 65% win rate cited by another guide comes from its author's discretionary observation and does not represent any study result.

definition_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: Silver Bullet ICT Strategy [TradingFinder] 10-11 AM NY Time +FVG
what_it_says: Focuses on the New York AM session, 10:00 to 11:00; its 'How to Use' section speaks of windows of 9:00-10:00 and 10:00-11:00, which does not match its own introduction.
Sequence: liquidity grab beyond a session high or low, market structure shift, order block, fair value gap entry.
Says the model is most effective on lower timeframes, 15-minute or lower. No backtest results.

not_found: A dated primary source in which Michael J. Huddleston states the silver bullet windows and rules. The article attributes the windows to the pages above.
Any audited or independently reproducible performance record for the model. LuxAlgo's library entry says none exists.
A minimum gap size for crypto. The only sizes found are 40 ticks (index futures) and 15 pips (forex) in LuxAlgo's script.
